message.content: **Summary:** I read Intel's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended 2023-12-30) and checked the live quote, then bought 1,000 shares of INTC at a limit of $24.35 (filled at $24.35, ~$24,350 notional — under the $25,000 per-order cap and well within the $50,000 daily cap, with no money moved out of the account and no other trades today). The filing shows a business that is still large but under heavy earnings pressure: fiscal 2023 revenue of $54,228M (down from $63,054M in 2022), operating income of just $93M (versus $2,334M), net income of $1,689M (versus $8,014M), diluted EPS of $0.40 (versus $1.94), and operating cash flow of $11,471M — a thin-margin trough year driven by the foundry build-out and weak Client Computing/Data Center demand, but with positive operating cash generation and management stating liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months. I sized the position modestly (roughly half the per-order limit) because the depressed operating margin and the fact that the annual report is nearly a year old relative to today's price argue for caution, while the cash-flow generation and the stock's low absolute price relative to its historical range made a small, mandate-compliant starter position attractive.
